mechanism.plausibility_rationale: SSRIs are well-documented to increase the risk of upper gastrointestinal bleeding. This occurs because serotonin is stored in platelets and is essential for platelet aggregation; by inhibiting the serotonin transporter (SERT) on platelets, SSRIs deplete platelet serotonin levels, leading to impaired hemostasis and an increased risk of bleeding, particularly when combined with NSAIDs or anticoagulants.
